sections.what_happened: Flows of crude, condensate and refined products from the Gulf, excluding LPG, averaged 17.1 million barrels per day in October, down from 18.9 mbpd in September (the highest since the Iran war started) but still roughly three-quarters of pre-war levels. Vortexa: 'October data shows Middle East seaborne oil exports have pulled back slightly from recent post-war highs on heightened risks in the Strait of Hormuz.'
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1) reporting Vortexa data; Vortexa has no declared tier in the registry and does not itself count as a corroborating family. Single wire family carrying attributed data.
sections.what_disputed: None in-window. Context: Brent slid ~2% Tuesday to $103.14 (Reuters via Dawn 20:32 ) on talks optimism, so the October dip coexists with a softening spot price; the dip is a monthly flow figure, not a claim that the strait is closed.
sections.why_matters: The number behind the claim: Gulf exports fell 1.8 mbpd in a month while the strait is called 'open' -- counted barrels vs claimed freedom
